newsitem.title: UK: British politician criticizes blonde nurses.
newsitem.headline: British politician criticizes blonde nurses.

text.p: A British member of parliament has sparked a race row in her east London constituency by saying hospitals should hire fewer blonde, blue-eyed Finns and more Caribbean nurses. "I am sure that these young women are charming. But they are basically here to improve their English and are unlikely to give the British health service a lifetime's commitment," Diane Abbott wrote in her local newspaper.

Abbott, a black Labour politician renowned for her outspokenness, expressed surprise that a hospital in her district hired "blonde, blue-eyed girls from Finland, instead of nurses from the Caribbean who know the language and understand British culture and institutions."
The column prompted several letters of complaint, according to the Hackney Gazette. Hospital officials have also written to Abbott outlining the severe staff shortages they face.
Senior nurse Eileen Farragher said 30 nurses from Finland had been hired to fill the shortage and another 20 were due in 1997.
"She didn't seem in any way to understand the facts," said Farragher. "The main area for recruitment has been Finland where, for whatever reasons, there is a surplus. It's been extremely successful."
